name: Eiffel Tower
description: Built for the 1889 Paris World’s Fair, this iron tower grew from an ambitious engineering project into a symbol of France. Its open lattice structure was assembled from more than 18,000 metal parts.

name: Colosseum
description: The Flavian emperors built this vast amphitheatre in the first century CE. Crowds gathered here for gladiator contests and animal hunts, making it a major venue for public spectacles in ancient Rome.

name: Stonehenge
description: Raised in prehistoric times, these enormous stones form a circle in the Wiltshire landscape. Together with nearby ancient sites, they offer clues to the beliefs and astronomical knowledge of the people who built them.

name: Statue of Liberty
description: France gave this monument to the United States, and it was dedicated in 1886. Standing at the entrance to New York Harbor, it became a symbol of liberty and a familiar sight for arriving immigrants.

name: Sydney Opera House
description: Opened in 1973, this performing arts landmark was designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon. Its overlapping shell-shaped roofs turn the edge of Sydney Harbour into a striking architectural silhouette.

name: Mount Fuji
description: This 3,776-metre volcano has inspired pilgrims, poets and artists for centuries. Its often snow-covered summit appears in celebrated Japanese woodblock prints, while shrines and pilgrimage routes connect the mountain to living traditions.

name: Taj Mahal
description: Emperor Shah Jahan commissioned this white-marble mausoleum in the seventeenth century in memory of Mumtaz Mahal. Its carefully balanced buildings and gardens stand beside the Yamuna River and reflect the craft of Mughal architecture.

name: Petra
description: The Nabataeans made Petra a crossroads for caravan trade. Buildings carved into rock sit among mountains and narrow gorges, combining local traditions with architectural influences from the Hellenistic world.

name: Chichén Itzá
description: This ancient Maya city preserves temples and monuments shaped by both Maya traditions and influences from central Mexico. El Castillo and the round observatory El Caracol are among its best-known surviving buildings.

name: Angkor Wat
description: Built in the twelfth century under King Suryavarman II, Angkor Wat began as a temple devoted to Vishnu and later became a Buddhist sacred site. Its carved galleries tell religious stories and record scenes from the Khmer kingdom.

name: Machu Picchu
description: The Inca built this mountain settlement about 2,430 metres above sea level. Stone walls, terraces and ramps follow the steep terrain, linking remarkable engineering with the surrounding mountain forest.

name: Great Pyramid of Giza
description: Built as the tomb of King Khufu, the Great Pyramid once had a smooth outer covering of fine limestone. It is the only surviving wonder of the ancient world’s traditional Seven Wonders.
descriptionSourceName: Egypt Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities

name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
description: Founded in 1395, Gyeongbokgung was the principal palace of the Joseon dynasty. Its halls and courtyards stand below Bugaksan; after destruction in the sixteenth century, the palace was rebuilt in the nineteenth century.

name: Merlion
description: With a lion’s head and a fish’s body, the Merlion brings together two images of Singapore. The original waterfront statue was unveiled in 1972 and became a familiar symbol of the city.

name: Brandenburg Gate
description: Built between 1788 and 1791, this sandstone gate brought Greek-inspired architecture to Berlin. A four-horse chariot crowns its columns, and the gate became closely associated with Germany’s division and reunification.

name: Belém Tower
description: This fortified tower stands beside the Tagus at the entrance to Lisbon’s harbour. Its carved stonework and corner turrets recall the maritime world of sixteenth-century Portugal.

name: Christ the Redeemer
description: Unveiled in 1931, this Art Deco statue stands on Corcovado above Rio de Janeiro. Its outstretched arms form a distinctive silhouette over the city’s forested hills and coastline.

name: Burj Khalifa
description: Opened in 2010, the 828-metre Burj Khalifa rises above central Dubai. Its tapering profile steps upward to a slender spire, while observation decks offer views across the city and desert.

name: Hagia Sophia
description: A landmark of sixth-century Istanbul, Hagia Sophia is celebrated for its vast dome and the space beneath it. It forms part of the city’s historic areas, where centuries of religious and architectural traditions meet.

name: Borobudur Temple
description: Built in the eighth and ninth centuries, this Buddhist temple rises through square terraces and circular platforms to a central stupa. Carved reliefs and smaller stupas turn the ascent into a journey through stone.

name: Great Zimbabwe
description: The stone ruins of Great Zimbabwe preserve a major Shona centre that flourished between the eleventh and fifteenth centuries. Its great enclosures and conical tower recall a city connected to long-distance trade.

name: Sagrada Família
description: Antoni Gaudí made nature a guide for this Barcelona basilica. Branching columns distribute the building’s weight like a stone forest, while geometric forms and coloured light shape its distinctive interior.

name: Moai of Rapa Nui
description: The people of Rapa Nui developed a remarkable tradition of monumental stone sculpture. These large human figures, known as moai, stand within a Polynesian cultural landscape of ceremonial sites on the remote Pacific island.

name: Great Wall of China
description: Successive dynasties built and linked fortifications across northern China, with construction continuing into the Ming period. Walls, watchtowers and mountain passes form an immense defensive landscape shaped by centuries of work.

name: CN Tower
description: Opened in 1976, Toronto’s communications and observation tower rises about 553 metres. A broad observation pod wraps around its slender concrete shaft beneath a long antenna.

name: Kinderdijk Windmills
description: Windmills, dykes and waterways at Kinderdijk tell the story of keeping low-lying land dry. The mill network belongs to a water-management landscape shaped over centuries for settlement and farming.

name: Hallgrímskirkja
description: Consecrated in 1986, this Reykjavík church was designed by Guðjón Samúelsson. Its rising concrete forms echo Iceland’s columnar rock, mountains and glaciers, gathering around a tall central tower.

name: Atomium
description: Built for the 1958 Brussels World’s Fair, the Atomium turns an iron crystal’s unit cell into architecture. Nine metallic spheres are joined by tubes, giving the structure its unmistakable geometric silhouette.

name: Petronas Twin Towers
description: Designed by César Pelli, these paired towers rise 451.9 metres above Kuala Lumpur. Their stepped profiles and slender spires frame a skybridge linking the two 88-storey buildings.

name: Shwedagon Pagoda
description: On Singuttara Hill in Yangon, Shwedagon is a major Buddhist pilgrimage site. Its gold-covered central stupa rises above terraces, shrines and pavilions, crowned by a jewelled umbrella.

name: Acropolis of Athens
description: Above Athens, this rocky hill preserves an ensemble of ancient Greek monuments. Major buildings from the fifth century BCE include the Parthenon, the Propylaea and the Erechtheion.

name: Saint Basil’s Cathedral
description: Built between 1555 and 1561, this cathedral stands on Moscow’s Red Square. Its clustered chapels and varied onion-shaped domes create a distinctive skyline whose appearance evolved over later centuries.

name: Ait-Ben-Haddou
description: This fortified settlement near Ouarzazate groups earthen buildings behind defensive walls and corner towers. Its compact hillside forms exemplify the traditional architecture of Morocco’s pre-Saharan region.

name: Sigiriya
description: A granite rock rises roughly 180 metres above the surrounding landscape at Sigiriya. The ruins of King Kassapa I’s fifth-century capital occupy its summit, approached by galleries and stairways through a monumental lion entrance.

name: Sossusvlei
description: Deep orange dunes surround a pale salt-and-clay pan in the Namib Desert. Sossusvlei formed where sand blocked the Tsauchab River; after exceptional rains, water can reach this usually dry basin.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
description: At 5,895 metres, Kilimanjaro is Africa’s highest mountain. Its volcanic massif rises above the surrounding plains, with forested slopes and a snow-covered summit forming a striking sequence of landscapes.

name: Prague Astronomical Clock
description: Mounted on Prague’s Old Town Hall, this astronomical clock combines timekeeping with a calendar and zodiac display. Its decorated dials and figures turn the tower wall into a miniature theatre of the sky.

name: Hungarian Parliament Building
description: This monumental home of Hungary’s National Assembly combines a richly detailed Neo-Gothic exterior with a prominent central dome. Rows of pointed windows and slender pinnacles give the long building its distinctive skyline.

name: Schönbrunn Palace
description: Schönbrunn developed from a hunting estate into the Habsburgs’ summer residence. Its broad yellow palace fronts an extensive garden landscape, bringing court architecture and formal outdoor spaces together.

name: Matterhorn
description: The sharply angled Matterhorn rises above Zermatt on the border between Switzerland and Italy. Its steep rock faces and snowy ridges make a striking pyramid-shaped outline in the Alpine landscape.

name: The Little Mermaid
description: Edvard Eriksen’s bronze sculpture has sat beside Copenhagen’s Langelinie waterfront since 1913. Inspired by Hans Christian Andersen’s tale, the small figure on a rock became an enduring symbol of the city.

name: Borgund Stave Church
description: Borgund preserves a distinctive example of Norway’s medieval timber churches. Stacked roofs, carved dragon heads and elaborate portals rise above wooden galleries, showing the craft of stave construction.

name: Helsinki Cathedral
description: Consecrated in 1852, Helsinki Cathedral is a central part of the city’s neoclassical monumental centre. Its columned portico, broad steps and domes create a recognisable silhouette above Senate Square.

name: Obelisk of Buenos Aires
description: Built in 1936 to mark four centuries since the city’s first foundation, the Obelisco stands where Avenida Corrientes meets Avenida 9 de Julio. Its slender shaft and pointed crown make it a familiar Buenos Aires landmark.

name: Walls of Dubrovnik
description: Stone walls and defensive towers surround Dubrovnik’s historic centre beside the Adriatic. Inside, churches, palaces and fountains recall the city’s long life as an important Mediterranean maritime power.

name: Boudhanath Stupa
description: Boudhanath is one of the Buddhist monument groups within the Kathmandu Valley World Heritage property. A great white dome supports a gilded tower marked with Buddha’s eyes, giving the stupa its powerful, simple form.

name: Ha Long Bay
description: Limestone islands and steep green towers rise from the waters of Ha Long Bay in northeastern Vietnam. Part of the Ha Long Bay–Cat Ba Archipelago World Heritage property, the seascape reveals karst shaped over a long geological history.

name: Hegra
description: At Hegra, Nabataean builders cut monumental tombs directly into sandstone outcrops. Decorated facades, inscriptions and wells preserve traces of a caravan city and its skilful use of the desert landscape.

name: Lotte World Tower
description: Rising 555 metres above Seoul, this 123-storey tower brings offices, homes, a hotel and cultural spaces into a slender vertical city. Its tapered silhouette combines modern glass construction with inspiration from traditional Korean forms.

name: Marina Bay Sands
description: Three hotel towers support a long rooftop SkyPark above Singapore’s Marina Bay. The elevated gardens and the dramatic overhanging deck make this waterfront complex recognisable as a group of towers joined by a ship-like crown.

name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
description: Built between 1993 and 1997 on a former industrial wharf beside the Nervión, the museum brought a new cultural use to Bilbao’s riverfront. Curved titanium surfaces catch changing light across its sculptural forms.

name: National Museum of Qatar
description: Jean Nouvel’s museum takes its interlocking forms from the desert rose crystal. Completed in 2019, the new building surrounds a restored historic palace and connects Qatar’s cultural story with its desert landscape.
descriptionSourceName: National Museum of Qatar official site

name: Heydar Aliyev Centre
description: Completed in 2012, this Baku cultural centre brings a museum, library and auditoria beneath a flowing roof. Its sweeping white surfaces rise from the surrounding plaza and fold around the spaces inside.

name: Baiterek Tower
description: Astana’s observation monument interprets the Turkic legend of the Tree of Life. A golden sphere rests above branching supports, recalling the egg laid by the mythical bird Samruk at the top of the sacred tree.

name: National Parliament House
description: Designed by Louis Kahn, Bangladesh’s parliament complex was built between 1962 and 1982 in Dhaka. Monumental geometric forms and the careful use of light give this modern civic building its distinctive presence.

name: Kigali Convention Centre
description: Opened in 2016, Kigali’s convention centre is recognised by its ribbed dome. The rounded form recalls a traditional Rwandan royal residence, bringing a local architectural reference into a contemporary gathering place.

name: Black Star Gate
description: Standing north of Accra’s Independence Square, this monumental gate is crowned by a five-pointed black star. It carries the words Freedom and Justice and commemorates Ghana’s independence; it is distinct from the nearby Independence Arch.

name: Biomuseo
description: Frank Gehry’s museum on the Amador Causeway celebrates Panama’s biodiversity. Irregular metal canopies in vivid colours shelter an open-air atrium, turning the building itself into a lively introduction to the country’s natural diversity.

name: Casapueblo
description: Artist Carlos Páez Vilaró shaped this seaside home and studio over decades at Punta Ballena. Its white walls, winding passages and terraces form a sculptural building whose museum preserves the artist’s work.

name: Taipei 101
description: Completed in 2004, this 508-metre tower rises above Taipei in stacked sections inspired by bamboo joints. Its eight-storey modules reinterpret traditional architectural forms in a glass-and-steel skyscraper.

name: Registan Square
description: Three madrasahs frame this historic square in Samarkand: Ulugh Beg, Sher-Dor and Tilla-Kari. Their monumental portals and tiled façades form an architectural ensemble at the heart of a city shaped by Silk Road exchanges.

name: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque
description: Inaugurated in 2001, this mosque in Muscat combines Indian sandstone with a large central dome and five minarets. Its prayer halls and arcaded courtyards create a spacious architectural setting for worship.

name: Kuwait Towers
description: This waterfront group of three towers forms part of Kuwait’s water-supply infrastructure. Slender shafts and blue-green spheres turn reservoirs and public viewing spaces into a distinctive silhouette above Kuwait City.

name: Bahrain World Trade Center
description: Two sail-shaped towers in Manama are linked by three bridges carrying large wind turbines. The design channels sea breezes between the towers, integrating renewable-energy equipment into the building’s architecture.

name: Sky Tower
description: Completed in 1997, Auckland’s 328-metre observation and communications tower has a slender concrete shaft, elevated public decks and a long mast. Moller Architects designed the tower as a prominent element of the city skyline.

name: Pyramid of Tirana
description: Originally opened in 1988 as a museum dedicated to dictator Enver Hoxha, this concrete pyramid was transformed into a cultural and learning centre in 2023. MVRDV added climbable steps and colourful rooms around its retained structure.

name: Palace of Parliament
description: Built during Nicolae Ceaușescu’s regime, this monumental palace in Bucharest combines broad terraces, repetitive colonnades and extensive ceremonial halls. Its architecture reflects a controversial project to concentrate state institutions in one vast building.

name: Rock-Hewn Churches of Lalibela
description: Medieval churches were carved downward into the rock at Lalibela. Trenches and passages connect this Ethiopian pilgrimage landscape; the cross-shaped Church of Saint George gives it a memorable silhouette.

name: Great Mosque of Djenné
description: The Great Mosque anchors the earthen architecture of Djenné, a historic trading town in the Niger inland delta. Its buttressed walls and projecting timber form a distinctive part of the townscape.

name: Leptis Magna
description: This Mediterranean city grew under the Roman Empire, especially during the reign of its native son Septimius Severus. Its surviving columns, public buildings and harbour reveal an extensive ancient urban landscape.

name: Amphitheatre of El Jem
description: Built in the third century, this Roman amphitheatre rises above the town of El Jem. Its tiers of stone arches and open arena preserve the scale of public entertainment in Roman North Africa.

name: Pyramids of Meroë
description: Slender pyramids mark royal burial grounds of the Kingdom of Kush near the Nile. Together with temples and settlement remains, they record a civilization connected with both Africa and the Mediterranean.

name: Arch of Trajan at Timgad
description: Timgad was founded as a Roman colony in AD 100 on the slopes of the Aurès mountains. Its monumental arch stands among the gridded streets and civic remains that make the ancient city plan readable today.

name: African Renaissance Monument
description: A monumental bronze-colored family group rises above Dakar on a coastal hill. The figures turn outward toward the horizon, making the sculpture a prominent modern landmark of the Senegalese capital.

name: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace
description: A broad dome and sweeping colonnades define this basilica in Yamoussoukro. Designed by architect Pierre Fakhoury with references to Saint Peter’s in Rome, it combines monumental religious architecture with landscaped grounds.

name: Mbanza Kongo
description: The former capital of the Kingdom of Kongo preserves traces of royal, religious and everyday life. Its surviving urban sites, including cathedral ruins, reflect encounters between Kongo traditions and European influences.

name: Rila Monastery
description: Founded around the legacy of Saint John of Rila, this mountain monastery became a major Bulgarian spiritual and literary centre. Arcaded courtyards and the nineteenth-century buildings surround its richly decorated church.

name: Old Bridge of Mostar
description: A high stone arch links the banks of the Neretva in Mostar. Destroyed during the 1990s war and rebuilt in 2004, the bridge is both an architectural landmark and a symbol of reconciliation.

name: Temple of Saint Sava
description: The Temple of Saint Sava is a prominent Orthodox landmark in Belgrade. A large central dome and smaller surrounding domes rise over its pale exterior, overlooking a public space used for gatherings and evening walks.

name: Bled Island Church
description: A church and bell tower crown the small island in Lake Bled. Reached across the water, the island combines a long religious history with a distinctive setting of lake, woodland and surrounding mountains.

name: Trakai Island Castle
description: Red-brick towers rise from an island in Lake Galvė at Trakai. The castle is associated with the medieval rulers of Lithuania, while restoration has made its courtyards and steep-roofed towers recognizable again.

name: House of the Blackheads
description: This ornate building faces Riga’s Town Hall Square and recalls the Brotherhood of the Blackheads, a historic merchant association. Its reconstructed facade pairs stepped gables with colorful architectural decoration.

name: Tallinn Town Hall
description: Tallinn’s medieval town hall stands beside the market square in the Old Town. A slender tower, steep roof and ground-floor arcade make the civic building a distinctive landmark of the Baltic trading city.

name: Paro Taktsang
description: Known as the Tiger’s Nest, this monastery clings to a cliff above the Paro Valley. Its white walls and golden roofs sit against the rock, creating one of Bhutan’s most recognizable sacred landscapes.

name: Wat Xieng Thong
description: Built in the sixteenth century near the Mekong, Wat Xieng Thong is an important monastery in Luang Prabang. Its low, sweeping rooflines and ornamental surfaces express the city’s temple-building traditions.

name: Wat Arun
description: Wat Arun stands on the Chao Phraya River in Bangkok. Its central prang and surrounding towers form an ornate skyline, reflecting a royal temple history that spans the Thonburi and Bangkok periods.

name: Badshahi Mosque
description: Commissioned under the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb, this mosque stands beside Lahore Fort. Red sandstone walls, pale domes and tall corner minarets frame an expansive courtyard.

name: Golestan Palace
description: The Golestan complex was a royal centre of the Qajar dynasty in Tehran. Its palaces and garden combine Persian craftsmanship with artistic and architectural influences from Europe.

name: Chinggis Khaan Statue
description: A monumental equestrian statue of Chinggis Khaan stands at Tsonjin Boldog, east of Ulaanbaatar. The bright metal figure and circular base create a striking modern silhouette against the open steppe.

name: Tikal
description: Steep temple pyramids rise above the forest at this major Maya city. Plazas, palaces and carved monuments preserve a ceremonial and urban landscape within Guatemala’s rich tropical ecosystem.

name: Copán
description: Copán was a major Maya centre whose plazas contain intricately carved stelae and altars. The Hieroglyphic Stairway preserves a long sequence of inscriptions, linking monumental architecture with royal history.

name: Joya de Cerén
description: Volcanic ash preserved a Maya farming settlement at Joya de Cerén. Houses, storage areas and traces of daily work offer an unusually close view of ordinary life rather than royal monuments.

name: Arenal Volcano
description: The steep cone of Arenal rises above the forests near La Fortuna. Protected within a national park, the volcanic landscape includes old lava flows and habitats that support Costa Rica’s rich wildlife.

name: Cartagena Clock Tower
description: The Clock Tower stands over a gateway into Cartagena’s walled city. Its three passages connect the old town with the surrounding streets, while the clock has become a familiar civic landmark.

name: San Francisco of Quito
description: San Francisco forms part of Quito’s historic religious architecture. Its church and convent reflect the artistic exchanges of the Quito school, where Indigenous craftsmanship and European traditions developed together.

name: Tiwanaku
description: This highland centre was the capital of an influential pre-Hispanic civilization. Monumental stone platforms, carved monoliths and the Gate of the Sun preserve its distinctive architectural and ceremonial traditions.

name: Sans-Souci Palace
description: The ruins of Sans-Souci stand near Milot in northern Haiti. Built after independence under Henri Christophe, the palace belongs to a group of monuments that express the ambitions of the new Haitian state.

name: Nan Madol
description: Massive basalt walls stand on artificial islets beside Pohnpei. Linked by waterways, this ceremonial centre records the power and building traditions of the Saudeleur dynasty in the western Pacific.

name: Papua New Guinea Parliament House
description: Papua New Guinea’s Parliament House draws on the country’s traditional architecture. Its bold roof form and carved decoration bring local cultural traditions into the setting of a modern national institution.

name: Royal Palace of Tonga
description: The Royal Palace stands near the waterfront in Nukuʻalofa, Tonga’s capital. The pale wooden residence and its landscaped grounds form a landmark associated with the country’s continuing monarchy.
